findings.title: Materials' 54-point lens gap is extreme
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.18x forward but 38.23x trailing, a 54-point percentile gap — the widest in the table. Analysts are underwriting 123 percent earnings growth, which would be a dramatic reversal from the reported earnings that put the trailing multiple at the 93rd percentile.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' cheap forward hides rich trailing
findings.body: Consumer Staples sits at the 50th percentile on forward P/E but the 89th on trailing, a 39-point gap. The 48 percent implied earnings growth is the second-highest in the table, yet the sector's forward multiple is only at its five-year median — a combination that suggests the market is not fully pricing in that expected expansion.

findings.title: Health Care's 86 percent growth is unbacked
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E is 18.76 at the 78th percentile, while its trailing multiple is 34.87 at the 77th — the lenses agree on valuation despite a 46 percent compression. That gap implies 86 percent earnings growth, an aggressive assumption for a sector whose forward percentile dropped 13 points in a month, signaling fading confidence in that forecast.
